findings.title: Empty update data never touches updatedAt
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty data object. Prisma updateMany with empty data is a no-op at best and throws a validation error at worst, and it does not trigger the @updatedAt bump. The intent in the comment is to refresh SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, but nothing is updated. Pass an explicit timestamp such as { updatedAt: new Date() }.

findings.title: Unfiltered credentialIds can crash cache status query
findings.body: credentialIds is built as connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId) with no filtering or deduping. If any entry has a null/undefined credentialId (delegation or in-memory credentials) Prisma receives an invalid value in `credentialId: { in: [...] }` and the whole connectedCalendars query fails. Filter to finite numbers and dedupe before calling getCacheStatusByCredentialIds.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired rows
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only considers rows with expiresAt >= now. A credential whose cache entries are all expired will still report a cacheUpdatedAt timestamp, so the UI shows Cache Status and offers Delete for effectively empty cache. Add the same expiresAt gte now condition.

findings.title: Cache deletion never refreshes cache status
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess, unlike disconnectMutation which invalidates connectedCalendars and integrations queries. After deleting cached data the enriched cacheUpdatedAt returned by connectedCalendarsHandler remains stale until a manual reload, so the user still sees the old Last updated timestamp and delete option.

findings.title: Generic Error leaks as internal server error
findings.body: When the credential is missing or belongs to another user the handler throws new Error("Credential not found or access denied"). In tRPC this becomes an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, hiding the real cause from the client which only shows a generic error_deleting_cache toast. Throw a TRPCError with the appropriate code.

findings.title: Dev script breaks on Linux and from repo root
findings.body: The script uses ENV_FILE="../.env" relative to the current working directory instead of the script directory, so running it from the repo root edits the wrong path. It also uses sed -i '' -E which is macOS-only syntax and fails on GNU sed/Linux. This makes the helper unusable for many developers. Resolve the env path via the script dir and handle portable in-place sed.
